answer: In an AI-agent market for grove mapping, willow pruning, and saffron harvesting, each seller must lock a separate token bond for 30 days before bidding. The same collateral cannot back two identities, and a cryptographically provable failure to deliver forfeits the bond. Creating names is cheap, but operating a thousand eligible agents requires a thousand bonds, tying up capital for a month and putting it at risk when the agents cheat.
